quiz.question_id: Apa konvensi penamaan factory function yang umum di Go?
quiz.question_en: What is the common naming convention for factory functions in Go?
options_id: `Create<Type>()`
`New<Type>()`
`Init<Type>()`
`Make<Type>()`
options_en: `Create<Type>()`
`New<Type>()`
`Init<Type>()`
`Make<Type>()`

quiz.question_id: Mengapa Go tidak punya constructor bawaan seperti Java/C++ menurut lesson ini?
quiz.question_en: Why does Go not have built-in constructors like Java/C++ according to this lesson?
options_id: Karena Go tidak mendukung pembuatan objek
Untuk menjaga bahasa sederhana, mendorong zero value yang berguna, dan memberi fleksibilitas lewat factory function
Karena struct Go selalu harus dibuat dengan literal
Karena constructor akan bentrok dengan garbage collector
options_en: Because Go does not support object creation
To keep the language simple, encourage useful zero values, and provide flexibility via factory functions
Because Go structs must always be created with literals
Because constructors would conflict with the garbage collector

quiz.question_id: Apa manfaat utama factory function seperti `NewPerson` dibanding membiarkan caller mengisi field private langsung?
quiz.question_en: What is the main benefit of a factory function like `NewPerson` compared with letting the caller fill private fields directly?
options_id: Factory function bisa memusatkan validasi dan aturan inisialisasi
Factory function membuat pointer menjadi immutable
Factory function menghapus kebutuhan method getter
Factory function membuat zero value tidak pernah dipakai
options_en: A factory function can centralize validation and initialization rules
A factory function makes pointers immutable
A factory function removes the need for getter methods
A factory function ensures the zero value is never used

quiz.question_id: Mengapa `NewPerson` pada lesson mengembalikan `(*Person, error)` daripada hanya `Person`?
quiz.question_en: Why does `NewPerson` in the lesson return `(*Person, error)` rather than just `Person`?
options_id: Karena Go tidak bisa mengembalikan struct by value
Karena pembuatan bisa gagal akibat validasi, dan pointer memudahkan berbagi/mutasi instance yang sama
Karena semua constructor Go wajib mengembalikan pointer
Karena `error` hanya bisa dikembalikan bersama pointer
options_en: Because Go cannot return structs by value
Because creation can fail due to validation, and a pointer makes it easy to share/mutate the same instance
Because all Go constructors must return pointers
Because `error` can only be returned together with a pointer

quiz.question_id: Apa yang ditunjukkan oleh `DefaultServerOptions()` dalam lesson?
quiz.question_en: What does `DefaultServerOptions()` illustrate in the lesson?
options_id: Pattern untuk menyediakan konfigurasi default terpusat yang masih bisa diubah caller
Satu-satunya cara membuat struct config di Go
Cara menggantikan semua factory function
Cara membuat field private menjadi public
options_en: A pattern for providing centralized default configuration that callers can still adjust
The only way to create a config struct in Go
A way to replace all factory functions
A way to make private fields public

quiz.question_id: Apa keuntungan desain zero-value friendly seperti `var s Stack; s.Push(42)`?
quiz.question_en: What is the benefit of a zero-value-friendly design like `var s Stack; s.Push(42)`?
options_id: Tipe langsung bisa dipakai tanpa inisialisasi eksplisit tambahan
Semua method menjadi static
Tidak perlu lagi pengecekan error
Semua field otomatis exported
options_en: The type is immediately usable without extra explicit initialization
All methods become static
Error handling is no longer needed
All fields become automatically exported

quiz.question_id: Kapan lebih masuk akal mengembalikan pointer dari factory function?
quiz.question_en: When does it make more sense for a factory function to return a pointer?
options_id: Hanya jika struct memiliki lebih dari tiga field
Saat struct besar atau caller perlu memodifikasi instance yang sama setelah dibuat
Hanya jika constructor menggunakan `fmt.Errorf`
Selalu, tanpa pengecualian
options_en: Only if the struct has more than three fields
When the struct is large or the caller needs to modify the same instance after creation
Only if the constructor uses `fmt.Errorf`
Always, without exception

quiz.question_id: Mengapa factory function cocok untuk field private seperti `name`, `age`, dan `email`?
quiz.question_en: Why is a factory function a good fit for private fields like `name`, `age`, and `email`?
options_id: Karena caller dari package lain tidak bisa mengisi field private secara langsung, sehingga constructor dapat menjaga invariant
Karena field private tidak punya zero value
Karena field private selalu harus berupa pointer
Karena getter tidak bisa dipakai tanpa constructor
options_en: Because callers from other packages cannot fill private fields directly, so the constructor can protect invariants
Because private fields have no zero value
Because private fields must always be pointers
Because getters cannot be used without a constructor

quiz.question_id: Apa tradeoff yang paling akurat antara constructor ketat dan zero-value-friendly design?
quiz.question_en: What is the most accurate tradeoff between a strict constructor and a zero-value-friendly design?
options_id: Constructor ketat memberi kontrol validasi lebih besar, sedangkan zero-value-friendly memberi kemudahan pemakaian langsung
Keduanya tidak bisa dipakai dalam package yang sama
Zero-value-friendly selalu lebih aman daripada constructor
Constructor ketat berarti type tidak boleh punya method
options_en: A strict constructor gives stronger validation control, while a zero-value-friendly design gives easier immediate usability
They cannot both be used in the same package
Zero-value-friendly is always safer than a constructor
A strict constructor means the type cannot have methods

quiz.question_id: Pernyataan mana yang paling akurat tentang constructor pattern di Go?
quiz.question_en: Which statement is most accurate about the constructor pattern in Go?
options_id: Itu adalah konvensi berbasis fungsi biasa, bukan fitur bahasa khusus
Itu keyword khusus yang wajib untuk semua struct exported
Itu hanya bisa dipakai jika struct punya field private
Itu menggantikan semua penggunaan literal struct
options_en: It is a convention based on ordinary functions, not a special language feature
It is a special keyword required for all exported structs
It can only be used if the struct has private fields
It replaces all struct literal usage
